title: Cache Locally, Recompute Selectively for Streaming Video Understanding
summary: FrameBlend replaces long-context idle-time prefill with short-window prefill plus query-time re-prefill of selected video tokens, whose recomputed KVs overwrite the stale cached entries. It costs an additional partial prefill pass at query time, adding latency and implementation complexity in token selection and cache replacement, though the paper reports this is outweighed by the prefill savings. It can fail when token selection misses query-relevant frames, when queries arrive too densely to amortize idle-time prefill, or with frameworks whose cache layouts do not support surgical KV replacement.
rationale: The method is training-free and plug-and-play on existing SVU frameworks, fitting a single-GPU budget, but its benefit is specific to streaming video workloads and requires validating token-selection quality and query-time latency on the reader's own traffic.
technique: Selective query-time KV recomputation for streaming video

claims.statement: FrameBlend replaces long-context idle-time prefill with short-window prefill plus query-time re-prefill of selected video tokens, whose recomputed KVs overwrite the stale cached entries. It costs an additional partial prefill pass at query time, adding latency and implementation complexity in token selection and cache replacement, though the paper reports this is outweighed by the prefill savings. It can fail when token selection misses query-relevant frames, when queries arrive too densely to amortize idle-time prefill, or with frameworks whose cache layouts do not support surgical KV replacement.

Over 20% reduction in per-frame prefill FLOPs on RVS-Ego and 14-59% lower total processing time for retrieval-based frameworks (including recomputation cost), plus accuracy gains up to 3.9 percentage points across three SVU frameworks and five benchmarks.
